short: The seven human STAT proteins - STAT1, STAT2, STAT3, STAT4, STAT5A, STAT5B and STAT6 - sit latent in the cytoplasm until a receptor-associated JAK kinase phosphorylates a single C-terminal tyrosine. Two phosphorylated monomers then pair through reciprocal SH2-phosphotyrosine contacts and clamp around DNA at a gamma-interferon activation site (GAS): the short inverted repeat TTCNNNGAA. Spacing is almost the only sequence feature that distinguishes them, with STAT6 preferring a four-base spacer and the rest a three-base spacer, so a GAS match names the family and not the member. STATs convert essentially every cytokine, interferon and several growth factor signals into transcription, and germline or somatic STAT mutations cause immunodeficiency, allergy, growth failure and leukemia.
long:
## The factors

Seven genes: STAT1, STAT2, STAT3, STAT4, STAT5A, STAT5B and STAT6. All share one architecture - an
N-terminal domain, a coiled-coil, a DNA-binding domain built on an immunoglobulin fold like those of
NF-kappaB and p53, a linker, an SH2 domain, and a C-terminal transactivation domain carrying the
conserved tyrosine. The protein is latent in the cytoplasm; a receptor-associated JAK phosphorylates
that tyrosine, and two monomers pair by reciprocal contacts between the SH2 domain of one and the
phosphotyrosine tail of the other, producing a C-shaped clamp that encircles the DNA. The
phosphotyrosine site of the SH2 domain is structurally coupled to the DNA-binding domain, so
dimerization and DNA binding are not independent. Which STAT is active is set by the cytokine, not by
the DNA: STAT1 homodimers by interferon gamma, STAT1-STAT2 plus IRF9 (ISGF3) by type I interferons,
STAT3 by the IL-6 family, STAT4 by IL-12, STAT5A and STAT5B by the IL-2 family, growth hormone,
prolactin and erythropoietin, and STAT6 by IL-4 and IL-13. STAT5A and STAT5B have no measured
difference in DNA-binding specificity.

## The motif

The GAS element is TTCNNNGAA: two TTC/GAA half-sites facing each other across a three-base spacer,
often written TT(N)5AA. Spacer width is the only substantial selectivity available. STAT6 prefers
four spacer bases, TTCNNNNGAA, but still binds three-base sites reasonably well; STAT1 and STAT5
prefer three, and STAT5A tolerates four weakly; none of them binds a lone half-site. In reporter
assays, a five-base TT-to-AA spacing is generally permissive, four favors STAT3-containing complexes
and six favors IL-4-activated complexes. Within the three-base class, STAT1, STAT3, STAT4 and STAT5
are not separable by sequence, and the consensus that the models here agree on, TTCCTGGAA, is
compatible with all of them. Two further arrangements matter in practice. First, tetramers: contacts
between N-terminal domains let two dimers bind tandem, individually weak GAS sites cooperatively, so
genuine STAT5 targets are often clusters of poor matches rather than one good one, and scanning for a
single strong site will miss them. Second, ISGF3: when STAT1 and STAT2 act with IRF9 they read an
ISRE rather than a GAS, with the STAT pair on the 5' GGAA and IRF9 on the second GAAA repeat. That is
why several STAT-labelled models here look like ISREs - HOCOMOCO STAT1.H14CORE.1.P.B
(TCAGTTTCRTTTTCC), HOCOMOCO STAT2.H14CORE.0.P.B (GGAAANHGAAACTGA) and JASPAR STAT1::STAT2.

## Where it acts

STAT occupancy is signal-dependent and transient: sites become occupied within minutes of cytokine
exposure and are vacated as the STAT is dephosphorylated and exported. Targets are both
cytokine-inducible promoters and, more often, enhancers, where STATs cooperate with the
lineage-defining factors of the responding cell. The practical consequence is that a GAS match in an
unstimulated cell type usually corresponds to nothing: the motif is present in the genome whether or
not the pathway is on. Type I interferon signaling shifts the element as well as the factor, from GAS
to ISRE, so the same STAT1 protein leaves different footprints depending on which interferon acted.

## Biology and disease

Human genetics has produced an unusually clear catalogue. Gain-of-function STAT1 mutations impair
IL-17 immunity and cause chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis. Dominant-negative mutations in the STAT3
DNA-binding domain cause hyper-IgE (Job) syndrome - a disease of DNA binding specifically, since the
mutant protein dimerizes but cannot read its site. Somatic STAT3 mutations, mostly in the SH2 domain,
occur in large granular lymphocytic leukemia, and activating STAT5B mutations recur in T-cell
leukemias. Loss-of-function STAT5B mutations cause growth hormone insensitivity with severe short
stature and immune dysfunction. Germline gain-of-function STAT6 mutations cause severe early-onset
allergic disease. Together these establish that STAT dosage and DNA-binding competence, not just
pathway activation, are rate-limiting in vivo.

## Reading a hit

Be conservative. TTCNNNGAA specifies only six bases, so it is expected on the order of several
hundred thousand times per strand in a 3.1-Gb genome; STAT matches are among the least specific in
this atlas, and this family is the least internally cohesive of the ETS/IRF/STAT group. The evidence
behind the models is also weaker than elsewhere: every HOCOMOCO model assigned here is ChIP-derived
(evidence letter P, grade B) with no in vitro HT-SELEX or methyl-HT-SELEX model, all nine JASPAR
models are ChIP-seq, six of them from mouse rather than human experiments (Stat2, Stat4, Stat5a,
Stat5b, Stat6, Stat5a::Stat5b), and two CIS-BP entries are transferred from mouse proteins on
DNA-binding-domain similarity - one of which is the motif this atlas selects as the family
representative. "This protein binds this sequence" therefore rests largely on in vivo co-occupancy
plus older in vitro studies. Expect confusion with IRF: the ISRE-shaped STAT models cross-match IRF
motifs, and in this atlas most nearest neighbours of STAT1.H14CORE.1.P.B, STAT2.H14CORE.0.P.B and
JASPAR STAT1::STAT2 are labelled IRF, while the JASPAR mouse Stat2 model's best match anywhere lies
outside the STAT family. The discriminator is orientation: a GAS is an inverted repeat (TTC facing
GAA), an ISRE is a direct repeat of GAAA. Finally, no STAT paralogue can be named from sequence -
STAT5A versus STAT5B is impossible - so use the cytokine, the time point and the cell type.
caveats:
A GAS match names the family, never the member: STAT1, STAT3, STAT4 and STAT5 read
the same three-spacer inverted repeat, STAT5A and STAT5B have no measured specificity difference, and
only STAT6's preference for a four-base spacer gives partial leverage. The element is short enough to
occur hundreds of thousands of times by chance, and occupancy is signal-dependent, so a hit in an
unstimulated cell type usually means nothing. Evidence is weaker here than for most families: all
HOCOMOCO models assigned to STAT are ChIP-only, all JASPAR models are ChIP-seq and two-thirds of
them are mouse, and two CIS-BP entries - including the family representative - are inferred from
mouse proteins. Expect overlap with IRF, since ISGF3 (STAT1-STAT2-IRF9) reads the ISRE, not a GAS.
